name: Roomantic: Furniture Planner
dev: Blank Slate Labs Limited Liability Company

ios.desc:
Scan your room. Paste a link. See the furniture on your floor plan at its exact real-world size — before you buy.

Roomantic turns your iPhone into an effortless room planner. A quick LiDAR scan captures your space and draws a clean, accurate floor plan in seconds. Then furnish it straight from the web: paste a product link from your favorite furniture and home stores, and the piece appears on your plan at its true measured footprint — photo, dimensions, and price included.

TRY BEFORE YOU BUY
• Paste a product link and Roomantic reads the item's real dimensions, then draws it to scale on your plan
• Drag, rotate, and rearrange with smooth, precise gestures — with full undo and redo
• Live fit warnings the moment a piece overlaps furniture, blocks a doorway, or sits outside the room
• A built-in cart tallies every planned piece with photos, prices, and store totals

SCAN IN SECONDS
• LiDAR-powered scanning captures walls, doors, windows, and furniture as you walk the room
• Precise measurements for every wall, door, window, and opening — automatically

NO LIDAR? DRAFT IT
• Draw any room by hand — set dimensions, place doors and windows, and start planning right away

UNDERSTAND YOUR SPACE
• AI-powered room analysis: area, dimensions, and insights about your space
• A calm, editorial design that keeps your plan front and center

SHARE AND EXPORT
• Professional PDF reports with floor plans and measurements
• PNG and DXF export for CAD and design tools
• Share any room as a private browser link — no app needed to view
• iCloud sync keeps your rooms up to date across your devices

Room scanning requires a LiDAR-equipped iPhone or iPad; drafting rooms by hand works on any device.

quotes.text:
Roomantic is a project I started working on earlier this year when I learned that iPhone Pro models have a LiDAR scanner and almost no practical apps that take advantage of it.

It uses Apple’s RoomPlan API to generate floor plans, and then allows you to paste in links to furniture and visualize if it would fit into your space.

Every feature is free, a subscription option exists if you want unlimited furniture placements (since those actually cost me money).

I tried my best to make the app beautiful, since features are now so cheap to build using AI, so any feedback would be appreciated.

It primarily supports U.S. retailers, but if there is any international interest, I’d be happy to build that out in the future.

Thanks!
